content:
Apple continues to improve the profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 regarding app access permissions gives users another reason to use profiles.

tvOS 27 lets you restrict users from opening specific apps

User profiles are a common feature on every major streaming platform. Among other benefits, they ensure that people living together keep their viewing history and recommendations separate.

Apple has had profiles on tvOS for a while, but over the past year, multiple updates have made them much more useful.

Now, tvOS 27 brings yet another improvement. According to Apple's official release notes:

This change is clearly designed for parents.

Kids profiles can already restrict the type of content they see in the Apple TV app. While useful, this doesn't stop children from opening other apps that don't have similar restrictions.

Now, however, parents can go into Settings and completely block specific apps from launching when a kids profile is active.

This makes profiles more complete, matching what users expect, and aligns with Apple's recent push to upgrade parental controls in iOS 27.

Speaking of profile improvements, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 will bring Apple's profile system to iPhone and iPad for the first time. You can read about it here.

Are you using profiles on Apple TV? What new features would you like to see added? Share your thoughts in the comments.
